description: Run a shell command or script on a runner in an execute session that allows shell jobs (a machine, say), with the runner's own tools, sandboxed. With tree_dir, the checkout goes along and the command runs in it; a runner with a workspace keeps installed dependencies between runs. Output streams as progress notifications if your client asks for them; the signed result (stdout, stderr, exit code, env with the tree and image it ran against) is returned at the end.

command.description:
The command to run, one word per element, e.g. ["pytest", "-x",
"tests/"]; quoted for the runner's shell. Give this or `script`.

files.description: Ids of file items to give the job, unpacked after the tree.

fresh.description: Start from an empty workspace on the runner.

labels.description: Run on any runner with a free slot that has all of these labels.

machine.description:
A machine added with `airlox machine add`, by name (`name/label`
also targets that label), instead of `session`.

memory_mb.description: Job memory limit in MB (default: the session's).

runner.description: Run on this runner (name or key).

script.description: A shell script to run instead of `command` (at most 64 KiB).

timeout_s.description: Job time limit in seconds (default: the session's).

tree_dir.description:
Send this checkout (a directory inside an allowed directory) as the
job's input, and start the job in it: the files git would commit or
add, ignored ones left out. A tree holding files whose names usually
mean credentials (.env, *.pem, ...) is refused: leave them out with
`tree_exclude` (sending them takes the CLI's --tree-allow).

tree_exclude.description: Globs of files to leave out of the tree.

wait_s.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the result (default 120, max 600; 0 to return at once).

name: run
